property_summary: The owner state variable must never be changed by a direct call to owned() by any non-owner; the mutant violates this by setting owner to msg.sender.
After any call to owned(), the owner of the reference contract remains unchanged, whereas the mutant may update the owner to the caller.
For any non-owner caller, a call to owned() must revert and leave the owner unchanged in the reference, whereas the mutant sets owner to that caller.
Any non-owner caller attempting to call owned() should revert, but the mutant allows any caller to succeed.
For any caller that is not the owner, calling owned() must revert; the mutant removes the require check, allowing non-owners to execute owned() successfully.
The reference C always allows the owner to successfully call owned() without reverting, while the buggy version always reverts for the owner.
Only the current owner can change the owner via transferOwnership; the mutant breaks this by allowing any caller to change it.
Only the current owner can successfully change the owner via transferOwnership; the bug allows any non-owner to change it.
A call to transferOwnership by the current owner always succeeds on the reference contract but reverts on the mutant, which only allows non-owners to call it.
After a successful transferOwnership call, the new owner must be the caller; the mutant inverts the access control so the caller can never become the new owner.

After any call to transferOwnership, if the caller is the current owner, the owner must remain unchanged; the bug inverts the guard, allowing non-owners to change the owner and disallowing the true owner from doing so.

After any call to transferOwnership(x) that does not revert, the ownership must have been transferred successfully (owner == x); the bug allows non-owners to cause a state change but then leaves the owner variable unchanged because the guard is inverted, so the caller can never set owner to themselves.
